title: Fundamental Principle of Counting
description: Sum/Product rule, Inclusion-Exclusion, Pigeonhole, Permutations & Combinations, Recurrence relations (LO4.1 - LO4.4)

questions.question: A student can pick a mini-project topic from 8 AI topics or 6 networking topics (no topic appears in both lists). In how many ways can the student choose one topic?
questions.explanation: The choices are mutually exclusive, so the sum rule gives 8 + 6 = 14.

questions.question: A menu has 4 starters and 5 main courses. How many different meals consisting of one starter and one main course are possible?
questions.explanation: Two independent choices made one after the other: 4 x 5 = 20 (product rule).

questions.question: Which rule is used when a task can be done in one of several ways and no two of these ways can happen together?
questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive alternatives are counted by adding the number of ways (sum rule).

questions.question: The product rule is applied when a procedure consists of
questions.explanation: If a procedure has steps done one after another, the total number of ways is the product of the ways for each step.

questions.question: If 11 pigeons are placed into 10 holes, which statement must be true?
options: Some hole contains at least two pigeons
Every hole has exactly one pigeon
questions.explanation: With more pigeons than holes, at least one hole contains two or more pigeons.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of people needed to guarantee that at least two of them were born in the same month?
questions.explanation: There are 12 months (holes), so 12 + 1 = 13 people guarantee a repeat.

questions.question: What is the minimum size of a subset of {1, 2, ..., 10} that guarantees it contains two numbers whose sum is 11?
questions.explanation: The pairs (1,10), (2,9), (3,8), (4,7), (5,6) are 5 holes. Choosing 6 numbers forces two from one pair.

questions.question: A bag holds many red, blue and green balls. What is the minimum number of balls to draw to guarantee at least 4 of one colour?
questions.explanation: Worst case 3 of each colour = 9 balls; the 10th ball guarantees 4 of one colour.

questions.question: Solve a_n = 2a_(n-1) + 3 with a_0 = 1.
questions.explanation: Homogeneous part A x 2^n, particular solution -3. a_0 = 1 gives A = 4, so a_n = 4 x 2^n - 3 = 2^(n+2) - 3.

questions.question: In how many ways can 4 married couples sit around a round table so that men and women alternate (rotations considered the same)?
questions.explanation: Seat the men in (4 - 1)! = 6 ways, then the women in the 4 gaps in 4! = 24 ways: 6 x 24 = 144.

questions.question: Five points are placed in a square of side 2. Two of them must be within distance at most
questions.explanation: Divide into four unit squares (4 holes). Two points share a unit square, whose diagonal is sqrt(2).

questions.question: By the Erdos-Szekeres theorem, any sequence of 10 distinct real numbers contains a monotone (increasing or decreasing) subsequence of length at least
questions.explanation: Any sequence of n^2 + 1 distinct numbers has a monotone subsequence of length n + 1. Here 10 = 3^2 + 1, so length 4.

How many subsets of a 6-element set have an even number of elements?
questions.explanation: Even-size subsets and odd-size subsets are equally many: 2^6 / 2 = 32.

questions.question: Which recurrence with initial values describes the number a_n of ways to climb n stairs using steps of 1, 2 or 3?
questions.explanation: The last step is 1, 2 or 3 stairs, so a_n = a_(n-1) + a_(n-2) + a_(n-3), with a_1 = 1, a_2 = 2, a_3 = 4.
